newsitem.title: USA: Gunman used motel receipt to buy gun in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Gunman used motel receipt to buy gun in Florida.

text.p: A Palestinian man who went on a shooting rampage at the Empire State Building used a motel receipt as proof of residency to obtain the state ID card which he then used to buy a gun, a state official said on Monday.
Ali Abu Kamal, 69, shot to death one tourist and wounded six others Sunday before taking his own life on the observation deck of the world-famous skyscraper.

Kamal, who lodged at the River Oaks Motel on U.S. 1 in Melbourne, Florida, from mid-January to Feb. 1, took the motel receipt and his passport to a state Division of Motor Vehicles office where driver licenses are issued.
He was issued a Florida Identification Card, which looks like a driver license but can only be used for identification, said Liz Hirst, spokeswoman for the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.
Kamal took the photo ID to the Oaks Trading Post, a gun shop a few blocks from his motel, where he paid $550 for a Beretta and $8 for a criminal background check.
"The background check only tells us whether someone has been convicted of a felony in the United States," Hirst said.
"For someone who had just entered the country, there's no way to tell whether they have a criminal record in another country," she said. "That wouldn't be in the computer."
At a news conference, New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani denounced the ease with which a foreign visitor to the United States could purchase a powerful gun.
Hirst said that anyone buying a gun anywhere in the United States is required by federal law to show that they have maintained residency for 90 days.
If Kamal got a gun after being in the United States just three weeks, he either lied or the background checks failed at the federal level, Hirst said.

Gary Gregory, manager of the River Oaks Motel, described Kamal's behaviour as odd. "I asked him one day if he was a terrorist, just kidding around, and he gave me a really odd look," Gregory said. "I never brought it up again."

A resident at the motel, Mike Ansen, said Kamal often stood in his open doorway naked, or walked around the motel room naked with the door and window open. "I think he might have been out of his mind," Ansen said.
